end.summary:
- Plotted/read an ordered pair using x-then-y movement.
- Identified quadrants from coordinate signs across three examples.
- Corrected the mix-up between (3, 2) and (2, 3) later in the lesson.
- Corrected the idea that a point on an axis must be in a quadrant.
- Practised axis placement; reflection was attempted but not completed unaided.
end.parentNote: Harsh practised reading ordered pairs, identifying quadrants from signs, placing points on axes, and distinguishing points such as (3, 2) from (2, 3). They initially mixed up the order of coordinates and included a point on the y-axis in a quadrant, then corrected both ideas later by explaining the x-then-y movement and the role of zero. At home, ask them to plot three ordered pairs and label whether each point is in a quadrant or on an axis.

नहीं, अलग-अलग जगह होंगे। तीन, दो मतलब x पर तीन और y पर दो, और दो, तीन मतलब x पर दो और y पर तीन। पहले वाले में एक्स ज़्यादा है तो राइट तरफ़ ज़्यादा जाएगा।

Haan, teen do aur do teen alag bindu hain: pehle mein x teen, doosre mein x do hai. Aapne kram ka fark saaf bataya. Ab x-aksh par mool bindu se teen ikai baayen jaayen, to us bindu ke nirdeshank kya honge?
